text:
maria_cs: flagging a Conflux onboarding: they're hitting intermittent 429s when their serverless workers call our /v1/chat endpoint. started after they ramped from 5 -> 80 concurrent warm invocations. logs attached by customer show a burst pattern.

maria_cs: sample from their logs: 
```
2026-02-18T14:12:04Z INFO request id=abc123 host=sdk.edge.conflux GET /v1/chat 200 time=120ms
2026-02-18T14:12:04Z WARN request id=abc124 host=sdk.edge.conflux POST /v1/chat 429 time=18ms x-rate-limit-remaining=0
2026-02-18T14:12:04Z INFO request id=abc125 host=sdk.edge.conflux POST /v1/chat 200 time=96ms
```

maria_cs: customer says they use ephemeral tokens per invocation (short TTL) + no client-side request coalescing. they're on our eu-west region.

dan_engineer: thanks, can you ask for their SDK version and the exact auth flow? ephemeral token-per-invocation is a red flag. also want to see their client code for token refresh.

maria_cs: they are on conflux-client-js v0.9.1, using serverless to request ephemeral tokens from their auth service on each invocation. shared snippet from them: 
```
// serverless handler
const token = await fetchAuthToken(); // called per request
await fetch("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat", { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
```

lee_se: yep—this will cause a preflight stampede. each invocation does a fresh handshake -> our token validation + early rate checks see the fanout. recommend: 1) cache tokens per container/runtime for token_ttl - 5s 2) add jittered splay on cold starts 3) enable keep-alive/connection reuse in their HTTP client.

lee_se: example quick patch for node: 
```
// naive token cache
let cached = { token: null, exp: 0 };
async function getToken() {
  if (Date.now() < cached.exp - 5000) return cached.token;
  const res = await fetchAuthToken();
  cached = { token: res.token, exp: Date.now() + res.ttl*1000 };
  return cached.token;
}
```

taylor_support: I'll coordinate a quick playbook with the customer and ask them to roll the cache + jitter change to a canary (~10% of traffic) today. maria, can you confirm they can expose the auth ttl on their token endpoint?

maria_cs: confirmed, auth endpoint returns { token, ttl_seconds: 60 } already. sent the patch suggestion.

dan_engineer: on our side, we can temporarily relax strict early rate enforcement for this tenant while they patch (low risk if we detect token-cache header). propose a 15-minute window with gentle backoff instead of hard 429. ops, can you open a short-lived mitigation?

ops_bot: created mitigation ticket #CS-4821. Owner: dan_engineer. Expires in 15m unless extended.

lee_se: additional SDK-level tweaks: enable http2 connection pooling and set `maxConcurrencyPerConnection: 16` if they use our SDK. also advise `prefetch=false` for warmers that are not long lived.

maria_cs: customer tried the cache patch in staging: their error rate dropped from 8% -> 0.6% in 20m. they will roll to prod canary now.

taylor_support: great. plan: 1) prod canary with token cache + jitter (10% traffic) 2) if stable for 30m, ramp 50% -> 100% 3) monitoring: we watch x-rate-limit-remaining and 429 rate via console dashboards. i'll post back.

dan_engineer: note: we should add a KB entry for ephemeral-token-per-invocation anti-pattern + suggested code patterns (node/python) and include a note on short TTLs causing stampedes. I'll draft and share.

maria_cs: customer happy. will close the ticket after full ramp. thanks all :thumbsup:

taylor_support: tagging @here in case infra sees surge after the ramp. I'll update in 45m.

ops_bot: ticket #CS-4821 updated: status=monitoring, playbook_applied=token-cache-mitigate, owner=taylor_support

maria_cs: follow-up: customer asked if we can expose a header that hints at token-refresh pressure (for telemetry). dan, is that doable?

dan_engineer: we can emit `x-auth-refresh-advice: cache-ttl=45s,suggest-jitter=true` from gateway for tenants who opt in. will spin a small feature flag experiment.

maria_cs: perfect — I'll capture that as feedback in the renewal notes (customer was nervous about risk before onboarding).

lee_se: note for retrospective: add a test in our integration harness that simulates 100 concurrent ephemeral-token requests to verify default protections.

maria_cs: closing loop: prod ramp finished, 429 rate back to normal. customer will include token cache in their onboarding checklist. closing this thread in 24h if no regressions.
